what_its_for: Fingolimod is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults and children 10 years and older. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows the worsening of MS symptoms. It works by keeping certain immune cells inside your lymph nodes so they cannot travel to your brain and spinal cord and cause damage.
how_to_take: Take fingolimod by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the regular capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. If you take the dissolving tablet (Tascenso ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve completely without water. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Your very first dose must be taken in a doctor's office or clinic so your heart rate can be monitored for at least 6 hours.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children who weigh more than 40 kg (about 88 lbs) is 0.5 mg once daily. Children who weigh 40 kg or less take 0.25 mg once daily. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you miss more than 1 day of doses, call your doctor before restarting — you may need to be monitored again like when you first started the medicine.
storage: Store fingolimod at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect it from moisture and light. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who have infections, especially chickenpox, shingles, or other contagious illnesses, because fingolimod weakens your immune system. Do not get live vaccines while taking this medicine and for at least 2 months after stopping it — talk to your doctor before any vaccination. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking fingolimod, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 months after your last dose. Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen, as fingolimod may increase your risk of skin cancer. Avoid starting or stopping other medicines without telling your doctor, especially heart medicines or other drugs that affect heart rhythm.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness (especially after your first dose); signs of infection such as fever, chills, body aches, or sores that do not heal; sudden vision changes or blurred vision; new or worsening weakness, numbness, or trouble walking; severe headache, confusion, or seizures; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); swelling of the face, lips, throat, or difficulty breathing (allergic reaction); or unusual skin changes such as new moles or sores that do not go away. Also call your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Fingolimod starts working in your body right away, but you may not notice a change in your MS symptoms for several months. Most people see a reduction in the number of relapses over time. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because it is working to prevent future flare-ups and slow down disease progression in the background.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use fingolimod if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious harm to your unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for 2 months after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Fingolimod is approved for children 10 years and older. Younger children should not use this medicine. Older adults: Use with caution; older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially heart and infection-related effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as fingolimod can affect liver function. Regular blood tests to check your liver will be needed. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have a slow heart rate, history of fainting, heart attack, or take medicines for heart rhythm, as fingolimod can slow your heart rate, especially with the first dose.
